context_requirements: Active JAK-STAT signaling, typically driven by autocrine/paracrine cytokines (e.g., IL-6 family) or oncogenic JAK/STAT activation
Expression of the relevant JAK isoforms (JAK1, JAK2, JAK3, TYK2) in the cell line
Presence of cytokine receptors that signal through JAKs (e.g., IL-6R/gp130, IFN receptors)
For antiproliferative/apoptotic effects, dependence on JAK-STAT for survival or proliferation
falsifiers: No decrease in STAT3 or STAT1 target gene expression (e.g., SOCS2, CISH, PIM1) at 6 h or 24 h in any cell line
No reduction in proliferation-associated genes (e.g., CCND1, MYC, CDC25A) at 24 h in cell lines with active JAK-STAT
No change in cytokine/chemokine genes (e.g., CXCL10, CCL2, MMP1) at 24 h
Strong upregulation of interferon-stimulated genes (e.g., ISG15, IFIT1) at 6 h, which would suggest an off-target or non-JAK effect

evidence.supports: Tofacitinib reduces synovial mRNA of MMP-1, MMP-3, CCL2, CXCL10, and CXCL13 in rheumatoid arthritis, indicating JAK inhibition suppresses inflammatory and matrix-remodeling genes.
AZD1480 inhibits JAK2/STAT3 phosphorylation and downregulates STAT3 target genes including Cyclin D2 in myeloma cells.
AZD1480 blocks STAT3 activation and decreases expression of STAT3 target genes including Cyclin D1, Cyclin D3, and CDC25A in pediatric solid tumor models.
Tofacitinib prevents cytokine-induced barrier dysfunction in intestinal epithelial cells, consistent with JAK-STAT inhibition in epithelial cells.

changes: Removed CXCL2, CCL2, and IL1B from proximal_up: JAK inhibition suppresses inflammatory chemokine/cytokine transcription, so these should not be listed as upregulated.

Removed generic proliferation genes CCNA2, CCNB1, PCNA, TOP2A, AURKA, AURKB, PLK1, UBE2C, and KIF20A from proximal_down; they are not proximal JAK-STAT targets and belong to generic proliferation effects.
Removed STAT1 and STAT3 from late_up: JAK inhibition reduces STAT activation and typically does not increase STAT1/STAT3 transcription.
Removed HLA-DRA, HLA-DMA, CD44, and ICAM1 from late_up: these are not established direct JAK-inhibition-induced genes and may be generic or context-dependent.
Removed IL13RA1, IL4R, and IFNAR1 from late_down: JAK inhibition does not consistently reduce transcription of these cytokine receptors.
Removed TGFB3, COL1A1, COL4A1, SPP1, and TIMP2 from late_down: these are not established JAK-STAT target genes and their direction is not justified by the cited evidence.
Kept MMP1 and MMP2 in late_down based on evidence that JAK inhibition reduces MMP expression.
Kept SOCS2, BHLHE40, IER3, DUSP4, DUSP6, ZFP36, NFIL3, TSC22D3, SPRED2, and TRIB1 in proximal_up as feedback/negative regulators consistent with JAK-STAT inhibition.
Kept CCND1, CCND3, MYC, and CDC25A in proximal_down based on evidence that JAK inhibition reduces these STAT3 target genes.
Kept BIRC5 in proximal_down as a STAT3-regulated anti-apoptotic gene.
Kept kinetics as slow and magnitude as weak at 6 h and moderate at 24 h, consistent with transcriptional effects of JAK inhibition.
Kept line_response with HT29 moderate and HA1E none; other lines weak, consistent with limited JAK-STAT dependence in most lines.
Kept evidence PMID 25398374, 21164517, 23531921, and 31751457; all abstracts support the stated claims.
